description:
Three clean records read in ascending key order, and the anchor that keeps this folder's field vocabulary honest (requirement I1). All 19 spans of app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy are named on every one of the three rows, so the field names are themselves part of the assertion: a translation that renamed a span, or that transposed two spans of equal width, is reported as a missing field rather than passing on bytes that happen to line up. The spans, 1-based and inclusive, with row 1's values - CUST-ID 9(09) 1-9 = 000000001; CUST-FIRST-NAME X(25) 10-34 = Immanuel then 17 spaces; CUST-MIDDLE-NAME X(25) 35-59 = Madeline then 17 spaces; CUST-LAST-NAME X(25) 60-84 = Kessler then 18 spaces; CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 X(50) 85-134 = 618 Deshaun Route; CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 X(50) 135-184 = Apt. 802; CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 X(50) 185-234 = Altenwerthshire; CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD X(02) 235-236 = NC; CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD X(03) 237-239 = USA; CUST-ADDR-ZIP X(10) 240-249 = 12546 then 5 spaces; CUST-PHONE-NUM-1 X(15) 250-264 = (908)119-8310 then 2 spaces; CUST-PHONE-NUM-2 X(15) 265-279 = (373)693-8684 then 2 spaces; CUST-SSN 9(09) 280-288 = 020973888; CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID X(20) 289-308 = 00000000000049368437; CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD X(10) 309-318 = 1961-06-08; CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID X(10) 319-328 = 0053581756; CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND X(01) 329 = Y; CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE 9(03) 330-332 = 274; and FILLER X(168) 333-500 = 168 spaces. They sum to exactly 500, so naming all of them asserts the total width by construction (gate G19) and proves the FILLER was emitted rather than trimmed away (gate G21).

The span that carries the point of the case is CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD at 309-318, held as 1961-06-08 by row 1, 1961-10-08 by row 2 and 1987-11-30 by row 3. app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy declares the same 10-byte span at the same offset of a near-identical 500-byte layout, but spells its name without the two interior hyphens - and the statement package models that copybook separately, as statement.model.Stm03CustomerRecord. Expectations written against that spelling belong to parity/CBSTM03A and parity/CBSTM03B; the hyphenated CVCUS01Y spelling is the only one that may appear in this folder, because collapsing the two would discard a name that field-for-field diffing depends on.

Two padding rules run in opposite directions here, and real fixture data pins both. CUST-ADDR-ZIP is PIC X(10) - alphanumeric, so it is padded with spaces on the right: row 1 holds 12546 followed by five spaces, while row 3 holds the full-width 19852-6716, a value no numeric picture could carry. CUST-SSN is PIC 9(09) and is zero-filled instead, which is why row 1's 020973888 keeps its leading zero. Reading those two rules the wrong way round would leave the record the right length and every value wrong.

Eight DISPLAY lines. The 38-character banner at app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:L71, then each record twice and adjacently - 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT displays it at L96 on a '00' status and the caller displays it again at L78 inside the same iteration of the L74-L81 loop, which is inherited behaviour and is preserved rather than tidied (practice B5) - and then the 36-character banner at L85. The fourth READ reports '10', which sets END-OF-FILE and emits nothing, so a fourth pair of lines would mean one record too many and a missing pair would mean one too few. Nothing is written and RETURN-CODE is 0: CUSTFILE is opened INPUT and app/jcl/READCUST.jcl:L6 is a bare EXEC PGM= with no PARM, so CustomerFileReaderJob is a job by name only (rule R1). Driven through that job's tasklet, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51), over the real CustomerService decision logic.

Statically derived, never executed. The expected values come from structured reading of app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl, the byte layout of app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy, the DD contract of app/jcl/READCUST.jcl and the three genuine rows of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt. They were not captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program, which is empirically impossible in this environment (practice B12; AAP 0.7.6, risk R-A).
